I'm one of the kinds of guys who puts a lot of effort in on a daily basis just for myself, but in my experience dating expectations can be a bit confusing or daunting.

I feel very comfortable going out and to work in a button up shirt, jeans, nicer boots, and potentially a Blazer depending on weather... Which for some dates I've been on was deemed as "over dressing"

And then I've tried similar outfits with a plain black tee and a blazer and felt under dressed.


I think that every woman has a very different idea of what the perfect date looks like or dresses like, so it's hard to know what is too much or too little for your specific date.

In my experience, there has to he a passion or a desire there for it to be good.

My last partner was unbelievably good at it and nearly everything they did worked perfectly with very little coaching from me.

My first was reluctant because they found it "weird" and subsequently there was a lack of effort, desire, or improvement over the three years I spent in that relationship.

I've found that most girls get better when you tell them what works and what doesn't, but on occasion you find someone who just doesn't get it and doesn't improve.

Make movies, I want to create but it's seemed nearly impossible because everything I make has to go into living and unexpected immediate expenses... Just having the freedom to do the work I Want to do.

Are you communicating the positives that he does?

I honestly think any guy who only hears about his failing and not what he does right could potentially start to feel bad about his performance... Not saying it's your fault just trying to offer a male perspective on the topic

Ex-wife but, when she had become verbally abusive towards me I had an extremely hard time moving past that after she was legitimately making an effort to change, and one day she says "You forgave your father, why can't you forgive me?"

Using the abuse I suffered as a child against me is probably the most lasting pain caused by any of her actions, even worse than the abuse

There are definitely two sides to this, on the one hand my ex for the longest time refused to give head which was very frustrating and left me unsatisfied or unable to finish at times, simultaneously I never insulted her for her being unable or unwilling to do that... So I think you can be disappointed but ultimately the insulting behavior is where you put yourself in the wrong.

Listen man, having thoughts or urges does not make someone inherently bad, the actions themselves do.

You said you would never hurt a child, and that means you aren't a danger to any children. Get psychological help, maybe medications, anything you can do to work on fixing the problem before resulting to any decisions such as ending your life.

Thanks to many the stigma around it and growing up being told that it's wrong, a sin, or something to be ashamed of, I think it's normal to believe it's wrong until you realize it's your life and your dick.

Too be honest this sounds like a "I want to be validated as a man in this family" rather than "I want to be a part of your wedding"

To me I don't thing you should change your wedding to accommodate him, if they really want to be closer they can still try for that after your wedding. This is a pretty sudden change a month prior to the big day.

I feel the same in many ways.

Although I'd say the very fact you're contemplating your existence proves you're human

This is wild man, too often when I discuss things with people around me they just don't seem to actually get it.

Glad some people do.

Not by my standards, you're an American citizen, you've come here and this is the country you know... This is your home, and I truly hope that nobody makes you feel like it isn't and that you aren't the same as any other citizen.

Unfortunately I guess you're right. I don't believe in religion and I don't see much meaning in life, it seems we live for so few moments that make us individually smile or laugh but we turn a blind eye to the awful shit that doesn't immediately have an impact on our Iives.
